We have a target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need retrosynthesis up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to propose route with templates.

We have one template from search: reaction_id 851565, retro_smarts_template: '[#7:3]-[C:2](=[O;D1;H0:4])/[CH;D2;+0:1]=[CH;D2;+0:5]/[c:6]>>O-C(=O)-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[#7:3])=[O;D1;H0:4].[CH3;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

Interpretation: This is a retro-aldol? Actually forward: O-C(=O)-CH2-CO-NH-CH=CH-aryl? Wait.

The product side: amide with trans-alkene attached to aromatic ring. The retro splits into a carboxylic acid (or ester?) and a methyl-aryl? Let's decode: product: [#7:3]-[C:2](=[O])/[CH]=[CH]/[c] (anilide with trans-alkene attached to aromatic). The retro yields O-C(=O)-CH2-... (i.e., a carboxylic acid attached to CH2) and a methyl-aryl (CH3-aryl). So the reaction is a Knoevenagel condensation? Actually O-C(=O)-CH2-... is a malonate? Might be a Wittig? Not sure.

But we can use this template to break the C=C double bond and amide? The product includes amide and trans-alkene. The retro splits into a carboxylic acid (or maybe acid chloride) and a methyl-aryl (like toluene). So we could propose disconnection: The fragment containing the amide and alkene (C=O-NH-CH=CH-aryl) can be formed by condensation of an acid (or acid derivative) with an aniline? Wait.

Better approach: Use simpler disconnections: The target has three main parts: (1) para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to phenyl sulfone (aryl-sulfonyl-aryl). (2) The sulfonyl phenyl is attached to a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we can think of two key steps: (A) formation of sulfonamide linking the two phenyl rings via sulfonyl chloride reacting with an aniline. (B) formation of the α,β-unsaturated amide via a Heck or Wittig? Actually we have C=O-NH-CH=CH-aryl (anilide). This could be formed by coupling of an aniline (anilide) with acrylic acid via amide coupling (i.e., coupling of 4-aminobenzoyl? Wait the amide is attached to the trans-alkene: C=O-NH-CH=CH-aryl. That's an enamide. Could be formed by condensation of an aniline with acrylic acid (or acryloyl chloride) to give an acrylamide, then isomerization? Actually the product is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-aryl? Wait SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So it's trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline (para? Actually it's an aniline with an NH2 at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with two amino groups? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino at position 1 and another at position? The ring has N at both positions? That's a diamino benzene (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide attaches to an aniline that also has an NH2 para to the amide? So the amide is attached to an aniline that also has a free NH2.

Thus we could form the amide by reacting acryloyl chloride with p-phenylenediamine (one amine forms amide, the other remains free). That seems plausible.

Then the sulfonamide formation: React sulfonyl chloride (derived from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) with the aniline (the other phenyl ring) to give sulfonamide.

Thus overall route: Step 1: Prepare p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial). Step 2: Couple with 4-aminophenyl (the phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide) to give sulfonamide intermediate (aryl-sulfonamide). Step 3: Couple acryloyl chloride with the remaining amine (p-phenylenediamine) to give the final product? Wait the sulfonamide intermediate still has the free amine that will be acylated.

But the target has the sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring that also bears the unsaturated amide side chain. So the order could be: Start from p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) and p-phenylenediamine? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to a phenyl ring (the tolyl) and the other phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated amide) is attached via sulfonyl group to the tolyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group, and the nitrogen also attached to the other phenyl? Wait SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (the first phenyl with methyl) and to the sulfonyl group, which is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (as substituent) and the sulfonyl group attaches to the second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the tolyl aniline (i.e., tolyl-NH-SO2-aryl). So we need to attach the sulfonyl group to the tolyl aniline.

Thus we need to start from p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) and a sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (i.e., 4-(... )-phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride could be made from the second phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain. So we could first make the second phenyl with the unsaturated amide (i.e., 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl). Then convert that phenyl to sulfonyl chloride (by sulfonation? Actually to get aryl sulfonyl chloride, you need to have a sulfonyl chloride group attached to the phenyl. That is not trivial from that phenyl. Better to start from sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and react with the aniline of the second phenyl.

Thus we need the second phenyl with a free amine to react with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride. The second phenyl is 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl. That phenyl has an amine (the aniline) that will be sulfonylated. So we need to synthesize that phenyl first.

Thus route: Step 1: Synthesize 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl (call intermediate A). This can be made by reacting p-phenylenediamine (commercial) with acryloyl chloride to give the enamide (trans). That yields 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). This is a simple amide formation (acyl chloride + amine). That's step 1.

Step 2: Sulfonylation: React intermediate A (which has a free aniline) with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (commercial) to give the target sulfonamide. That's step 2.

Thus total 2 steps (both are single-step reactions). Leaves: p-phenylenediamine, acryloyl chloride, p-tolylsulfonyl chloride. All commercially available. Need to verify price total < $9999. Likely yes.

We need to provide route JSON with reaction templates. We need template IDs for amide formation (acyl chloride + amine) and sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). We need to search for templates.

Search for amide formation: functional_groups_formed: ["amide"], maybe also bonds_formed: ["C-N"].
